Lessons.Title: Number Talk
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use patterns, structure, and understanding of properties of operations to design a series of expressions for a Number Talk activity.
This lesson provides an opportunity to listen to ways in which you make use of structure and repeated reasoning to design a Number Talk. In the warm-up, you are given a typical Number Talk with four expressions and discuss how the expressions are related. In the first activity, you practice anticipating the different ways someone might reason about addition and subtraction for a group of expressions and create expressions that would fit with the given string of expressions.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Number Talk: A Whole Number and a Fraction (10 minutes); Activity 1: Related Numbers, Related Expressions (20 minutes); Activity 2: Add One New Expression, Then Two (15 minutes); Activity 3: Add Three New Expressions [OPTIONAL] (30 minutes); Cool-down: Reflection (5 minutes)
Math focus: A Number Talk builds a purposeful series of related expressions so mental strategies and operation properties become visible.

Worked Edulytics example: 15 + 29 = 44. Double both addends to get 30 + 58 = 88, exactly double the original sum. Explain the distributive property of doubling an entire sum rather than memorizing unrelated totals. Create one further related expression and justify the pattern.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): Find 18 + 27 and 36 + 54 mentally; explain the relationship.
